issues.failure_explanation: The abstract promises a generalized difference variational bicomplex for non-uniform meshes. But the generalized exterior difference $\sum_i \Delta^i_n \wedge D_i/\epsilon^i_n = \sum_i \epsilon^i_n \Delta^i \wedge D_i/\epsilon^i_n = \sum_i \Delta^i \wedge D_i$ reduces identically to the uniform-case operator because the step sizes cancel trivially. The bicomplex is the same as the uniform one. Furthermore, both numerical examples explicitly use uniform step sizes, so no non-uniform mesh integrator is actually analyzed.

failure_location.quote: we demonstrate  how multisymplectic integrators can be comprehended even on non-uniform meshes through a generalized difference variational bicomplex.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the scope claims: remove or qualify 'generalized' and 'non-uniform meshes' in the abstract and section title, acknowledging that the operators are identical to the uniform case and that the examples use uniform step sizes.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope claim that multisymplectic integrators are comprehended on non-uniform meshes via a generalized bicomplex is not supported. The formalism provides no new content beyond the uniform case.
issues.title: Non-uniform mesh generalization is trivial and examples use uniform meshes
issues.why_classification: The formalism and examples are mathematically correct as they stand; only the scope/achievement claims need revision. No substantive result or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The exterior difference $\dDh = \sum_i \Delta^i \wedge (S_i - \mathrm{id})$ depends on the specific shift operators $S_i$. Under a GL(2,ℤ) change of coordinates such as $n'^1 = n^1+n^2,\; n'^2 = n^2$, the new forward differences are $D'_1 = S_1 - \mathrm{id}$ and $D'_2 = S_2 S_1^{-1} - \mathrm{id}$. The Lie differences $S_i - \mathrm{id}$ do not transform as vectors under GL(p,ℤ) (unlike continuous total derivatives), so $\dDh$ is not coordinate-free. A concrete counterexample: applying $\dDh$ to $f=(n^1)^2$ gives $(2n^1+1)\Delta^1$ in original coordinates but $(2n^1+1)\Delta'^1 + (-2n^1+1)\Delta'^2$ in new coordinates, which are unequal for any consistent transformation of $\Delta'^i$.

failure_location.quote: Both $\dDh$ and $\dv$ are invariant under all allowable changes of the coordinates used to describe their respective spaces, namely $GL(p,\mathbb{Z})$ transformations of the base space $\mathbb{Z}^p$ and diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^q$ (prolonged to $\mathbb{Z}^p\times P(\mathbb{R}^q)$).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the group of allowed coordinate changes to translations (or a subgroup of GL(p,ℤ) for which the Lie differences transform compatibly) and revise the remark accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the difference variational bicomplex is a coordinate-free geometric object invariant under GL(p,ℤ) is undermined. All formal results proved in fixed coordinates survive.
issues.title: GL(p,ℤ) invariance of the exterior difference is false
issues.why_classification: Restricting the coordinate-change group preserves every formal result (proved in fixed coordinates) but necessarily withdraws the advertised GL(p,ℤ) geometric invariance, a limited weakening.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity σ = I^Δ(σ) − D^Δ_h τ is stated in Section 3 as a consequence of exactness of the difference bicomplex. But the proofs of exactness (Theorems 3 and 4 in the appendix) use this very identity (via \eqref{eq:ii} or its difference analogue). The reasoning is circular: exactness is used to derive the identity, and the identity is used to prove exactness. The identity itself is a discrete summation-by-parts result that can be proved directly, but no such proof is given.

failure_location.quote: As $\mcI^{\vartriangle}$ is a projection and the difference variational bicomplex is exact, a difference version of equality \eqref{eq:ii} holds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove σ = I^Δ(σ) − D^Δ_h τ directly by multi-index summation by parts (the discrete analogue of integration by parts), before invoking it in the proofs of exactness.
issues.overall_effect: The proofs of horizontal exactness (Theorem 3), boundary-complex exactness (Theorem 4), and the coordinate-free Noether conservation law (eq:Noecl) all rely on the unestablished decomposition and are unreliable as written.
issues.title: Circular justification of the difference analogue of the decomposition σ = I(σ) − d_h τ
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a contained nontrivial summation-by-parts argument but no new proof architecture. Once established, all downstream results follow.

issues.failure_explanation: Two structural claims are asserted without proof. First, any vertically closed (p−1,2)-form ω with D^Δ_h ω = 0 on solutions of a first-order PΔE is claimed to have the 'standard' representation with vertical 2-forms d_v(S_i^{-1}u^α)∧d_v u^β. A general such ω has vertical 2-forms d_v u^α_J∧d_v u^β_K for arbitrary multi-indices J,K and need not have this restricted form. Second, the reconstructed Lagrangian is claimed to be of the specific form (lp) (first-order, linear in D^Δ_h u), which is not established. Additionally, the claim that λ_ξ = σ_ξ − v_ξ⊣η satisfies the multimomentum-map condition d_v λ_ξ = v_ξ⊣ω (equivalently d_v σ_ξ = L_{v_ξ}η) is asserted but not proved.

issues.failure_explanation: The homotopy identity h_h^{k+1,l}(D^Δ_h σ) + D^Δ_h(h_h^{k,l}(σ)) = σ is claimed for 1 ≤ k ≤ p. At k = p, since D^Δ_h σ = 0 for all σ ∈ Ω^{p,l}, the identity reduces to D^Δ_h(h_h^{p,l}(σ)) = σ, asserting that every (p,l)-form is a horizontal divergence. This is false: the horizontal row is not exact before augmentation (ker I^Δ is a proper subspace of Ω^{p,l}). For instance, with p=1, l=1, the form σ = f(n,u) Δ¹∧d_v u₀ satisfies I^Δ(σ)=σ and is not in im(D^Δ_h), while the homotopy formula gives h_h^{1,1}(σ)=0, so D^Δ_h(h_h^{1,1}(σ)) = 0 ≠ σ.
